text: Less than a week ago our 98th Electron delivered mission success for hawkeye360 with another flawless launch. Up next: Our 99th launch is scheduled next week and our 100th rocket is close behind, scheduled for delivery to Launch Complex 1 soon.

Make parts that go to space 🚀 We’re hiring CNC Operators and Programmers in Auckland, New Zealand, and Long Beach, CA. Be part of the high performance team bringing designs for spacecraft and rockets to life using advanced manufacturing technology.

Neutron’s Stage 2 and Thrust Module have arrived to Virginia. After a short barge ride from the Neutron Factory, these major assemblies have now been offloaded on Wallops Island and are going through arrival checkouts. Next up: integrated fluids testing and launch mount interface checkouts for the Thrust Module, with Stage 2 to follow on the test stand beside it soon after.
Enjoy the sights and sounds of shipping Neutron's Stage 2 and Thrust Module to Launch Complex 3.

Members of SemperCitiusSDA's Tranche 2 leadership team were recently at Rocket Lab's California headquarters to see T2TL-Beta in production. Eight of 18 spacecraft are on the floor right now, in build. Solar panels, structures, star trackers, reaction wheels, radios, flight software, avionics, launch dispenser — all built in-house. Proliferated architectures demand production at scale. Rocket Lab is all in on SDA's mission, and the action on our floor proves it. We're proud to be delivering this.

Every 8 days an Electron rocket rolls off the production line thanks to our mission-obsessed team and advanced factories. The Electron team is growing as we prepare to launch more rockets than ever before in 2027. Role open across vehicle assembly, composites, GNC, propulsion, manufacturing engineering, software, and more. Those with automotive, aerospace, marine, aviation, and manufacturing experience are a great fit. Come to New Zealand and Long Beach, CA to design, build, test, and launch rockets. Relocation support available. Adventure awaits: https://t.co/F3ZNC0C0B2

It’s a beautiful day to set sail with the next pieces of Neutron flight hardware to Launch Complex 3. Earlier today we sent Neutron’s Stage 2 and Thrust Module out of the Neutron Factory and onto a barge for transport through Chesapeake Bay to Wallops Island in Virginia. Once it arrives, the Thrust Module will go straight onto the launch mount at LC-3 for check outs and the beginning of wider systems demonstrations including integrated fluids tests and module-to-launch-mount interface checkouts. With no strongback on the launch mount by design, Neutron’s Thrust Module is the rocket’s only physical interface to the launch pad, which this upcoming test campaign enables us to test early before the entire vehicle comes together.
